newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wayss & Freytag eyes stronger developments.
newsitem.headline: Wayss & Freytag eyes stronger developments.

text.p: German construction group Wayss & Freitag AG will likely show an operating loss for 1996, but a broad restructuring has paved the way for healthy developments in the medium-term, the group's chief financial officer said.

Reinhardt Gennies told Saturday's Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung that the group, now 74 percent-owned by Dutch group HBG, recorded 1996 construction output near year-ago levels, or just slightly above three billion marks.
But Gennies predicted the group would likely post an operating loss for 1996 despite strong business abroad. In 1995 the group posted a net profit of 25 million marks.
Strong international demand helped boost 1996 orders in hand by nine percent to about 3.2 billion marks, he said.

The group's workforce shrank by two percent to 7,900 people last year, with most of the job losses occurring in Germany. More jobs are likely to be shed this year, he added. Last year the group created new jobs abroad.
Gennies said the group's restructuring should help create improved conditions.
